ITEM.PTXT: Stainless steel exhaust manifold and exhaust pipes have been adopted to reduce weight and improve corrosion resistance.

Three-way catalysts are located directly below the exhaust manifold (integrated with the exhaust manifold) to reduce emissions immediately after engine start (when cold), and are also located in the center pipe, ensuring sufficient emission performance to comply with "75% reduction level from the 17 emission standards (SU-LEV)".

The A/F sensor is located upstream of the three-way catalyst in the exhaust manifold, and the O2sensor is located downstream of the three-way catalyst in the exhaust manifold, enabling precise air-fuel ratio control.

By adopting a stainless steel sheet exhaust manifold, weight has been reduced and corrosion resistance improved, and catalyst warm-up immediately after engine start has been accelerated to reduce emissions.
A three-way catalyst integrated with the exhaust manifold has been adopted. This accelerates warm-up of the catalytic converter, improving emission performance immediately after engine start.
A heat insulator has been provided to cover the entire manifold. Also, holes have been provided to cool the manifold, achieving both protection of surrounding parts and cooling of the manifold.

By setting the exhaust gas entry angle between the exhaust manifold and three-way catalyst to 0° and enlarging the cross section of the pipe junction, the exhaust gas flow has been smoothed to improve performance.
Stainless steel exhaust pipes with excellent heat resistance have been adopted.
Compact ball joint mechanisms have been adopted between the exhaust manifold and front pipe and between the center pipe and tail pipe, reducing booming noise in the vehicle, weight and vibration.

The ball joint mechanism consists of a flange with a spherical surface, and bolts and springs that support the seal portion of the gasket. Compared to a flexible pipe, it can be made more compact and can be installed at the optimum position with respect to vibration.
Vibration and noise are reduced by absorbing vibration from the engine and resonance vibration of the exhaust pipe with the ball joint (spherical portion of the flange and gasket).

A 2WAY exhaust system has been adopted for the main muffler to improve exhaust efficiency and engine output while ensuring quietness. In the 2WAY exhaust system, a variable valve that adjusts the exhaust gas passage area according to exhaust gas pressure is provided inside the main muffler. The variable valve is kept closed by a return spring during idling and at low engine speeds.
By adopting a sub muffler with integrated catalyst on 4WD models, underfloor space has been secured and exhaust silencing effect has been improved.

ENTRY.PTXT: Since the exhaust gas pressure in the main muffler is low, the variable valve is closed, and the muffler functions as a muffler that emphasizes silencing to reduce booming noise.

When the exhaust gas pressure in the main muffler increases as the engine speed increases, the variable valve opens to enlarge the passage, and the muffler functions as a low back pressure, high output type muffler.
